title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is a 64-year-old individual presenting for a routine follow-up regarding their type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports consistent adherence to their long-term insulin regimen. They currently do not take any oral medications for glucose management. The patient also reports ongoing symptoms of peripheral neuropathy, characterized by occasional tingling and numbness in the lower extremities. The patient states that these symptoms have been stable over the last three months.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination reveals intact sensation in the upper extremities. Lower extremities show diminished sensation to monofilament testing in the toes. No new skin breakdown or ulcers noted.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on insulin therapy.
2. Polyneuropathy: The patient presents with symptoms of polyneuropathy. It is noted that this condition is not related to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. Monitor blood glucose levels. Follow up in three months for routine evaluation.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
